independent_variables.name: MACVAR
independent_variables.definition: First principal component of four macroeconomic-variability proxies: country-year median of the five-year standard deviation of annual EPS scaled by total assets per share; five-year standard deviation of accounting ROE; standard deviation of residuals from an annual GDP-growth-on-time-index regression over the sampling period; and coefficient of variation of yearly average US-dollar/local-currency exchange rates. Numerical component loadings and other PCA implementation details are not reported.
independent_variables.formula: PC1(SD(annual EPS over five years) scaled by total assets per share; SD(accounting ROE over five years); SD(residuals from annual GDP growth regressed on a time index); coefficient of variation of yearly average US$/local-currency rates); loadings unreported.

evidence.quote: MACVAR is the first principal component of four proxies for macroeconomic variability

we consider four variables: (1) the standard deviation of annual earnings per share over the last five years scaled by total assets per share, (2) the standard deviation of accounting returns on equity over the last five years, (3) the standard deviation of the residuals from a regression of annual gross domestic product (GDP) growth rates on a time index over the sampling period, and (4) the coefficient of variation of yearly average exchange rates (US$ to local currency) over the sampling period.
We therefore summarize the four variables into a single control variable for macroeconomic variability using the first principal component.
The first two variables are based on firm-level data, but like all other variables they are measured as country-year medians.

scope.quote: we investigate whether the effectiveness of securities regulation and supporting legal institutions are systematically related to firms’ cost of equity capital, over and above traditional proxies for firm and country risk.

The results indicate that these institutional proxies are significantly related to international differences in the cost of equity capital over and above traditional proxies for firm and country risk.
In most of our analyses, we simultaneously include disclosure regulation ( DISREQ ) or securities regulation ( SECREG ) together with the rule of law variable ( LAW ).
The first five models in table 4 present results using the full set of controls from model 3 in table 3.
As mentioned above, we extend our analysis by including DISREQ or SECREG in conjunction with the LAW variable.

review_notes: Final source-first scope: Table 4 columns 4–5 are the principal full-control regressions for the effect of securities regulation over and above overall legal-system quality: rAVG on DISREQ plus LAW, and rAVG on SECREG plus LAW. The source says most analyses include one securities measure with LAW, because the constructs are sufficiently distinct and the specification estimates the securities-regulation effect beyond legal-system quality.

Columns 1–3 show separate institutional associations and are excluded as less complete specifications for this question; columns 6–7 use reduced control sets; columns 8–9 use the accuracy-weighted rWEIGHT outcome. Later growth sensitivity, robustness, and capital-market-integration analyses are also outside scope.

The retained MACVAR control includes a GDP-growth residual-variability component, so its actual trend regression remains a supporting dependency. The PCA and implied-cost-of-capital IRR calculations are not regressions.
